VaultAge Solution Bitcoin scam

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Vaultage Solutions owned by Willie Breedt reputable businessman from Krugersdorp who also owned the local community newspaper Westrand News, a mansion in the upmarket estate of Featherbrooke Estate, and a drone business. Willie loves Harley Davidsons and smart cars and is a flash friendly guy. Since 2018 he’s convinced 2500 people to invest R227 Million in his Bitcoin Business. In December 2019 he threw a big end of year function to celebrate how well they were all doing, now he is holed up in Jeffreys bay and investors are no longer getting their weekly 5% interest pay-outs, never mind their original capital investments. Was this just another pyramid scheme gone belly up?

Summary:
With the local economy looking more and more rocky it was a fail-safe investment because the trading was done by an ‘Automated Trading System’ programmed never to trade when the prices were down and half the money was in a hedge fund so nobody’s capital was at risk. Investors would earn 20% a month interest and they could withdraw 5% a week. Many people made good money over the last two years but then in September last year Willie started to pay people late and from January this year nobody is seeing any money just lots of empty promises.
Initially investors thought he had left the country when he went to Mozambique in December and it was clear he had left Krugersdorp. Then he had a nervous breakdown and his wife asked investors just to be patient, holed up in Jeffreys Bay in another exclusive estate, a home which he bought for cash for R3.8 million but ensured he registered in a family trust is his bolt hole. Since April he has made a series of promises that he will pay out 70% of people capital investments, none of which have transpired. Fears that he may leave the country as soon as lockdown has eased has spurred 200 of the investors to hire an attorney who is bringing an urgent application this Wednesday 17th June.



Further information:
The other major culprit in this scheme is Anton Rogers was a financial broker for Liberty Life has been advising his clients since September 2018 to move their Liberty investments into Vaultage Solutions. With several years’ experience and various financial degrees, you could trust his word. He convinced 774 of his clients including his mother, his cousins that Vaultage Solutions was a great way to increase your investments. He earned commission from Willie Breedt but when his clients confront him he says he is just another investor and also a victim. He was fired by Liberty Life in January 2020 and is now recruiting people to invest in the latest pyramid scheme Crowd 1. Anton lives in Pretoria.
Willie Breedt has done this before, another financial investment scheme called MSM and Bitcoin Global which involved 23 billion rand went under and Willie was convicted of convicted on a criminal charge of fraud and was given a sentence of six years imprisonment, five of which are suspended . He is currently still on a suspended sentence which expires September 2020 and if found guilty again on another charge can go to prison for the full suspended term of 5 years. Vaultage solutions is not registered in terms of Section 5 of the Collective Schemes Control Act, 45 of 2002, with the Financial Sector and Vaultage Solution was only registerd as a company in April 2019 with Willie as the sole director. If you are convicted of fraud you cannot be the director of a company and seems like he only registered the company after trading for at least 6 months.
In September when Willie started to pay out dividends later and later and it became apparent his data base was in complete disarray. By December he had left Krugersdorp for his house in Jeffreys bay. He has met several of his investors who drove to Jeffreys Bay to negotiate with him. We have a video of his negotiating with Dr Bertus Jansen van Vuuren that he will hand over his luxury cars if he can’t pay his debt.


Extra Budget Items:
There is still a possibility that I will have to drive to PE but there doesn't seem to be accommodation.At this stage Denis Godard will go film the zoom call with Willie Breedt which will be 160 kms round trip at R3.50 per km so R560.00 for Jeffreys travel.
The Johannesburg/Pretoria/ Krugersdorp trips are 250 kms and there will have to be two vehicles, Masa and Siniketiwe in one, Dan and Camera assistant in the other. So that R875 per car R1750 total. I have to pay for 3 crew days and gear which makes this this expensive for me so would appreciate the help covering the travel costs
I will travel 80km round trip to film the zoom interview with the Bitcoin expert but I will pay for my travel

Script:


Link: Times are tough, so one can’t blame people for trying to make their money grow especially when the returns are so good, and the dollars look promising in their online wallets
Script: Vaultage Solutions was selling a failsafe cryptocurrency investment. CEO Willie Breedt claimed he owned the licence for a trading bot programmed with algorithms that ensured it never traded when the markets were down, removing the risks of human error. But what really sold it for most people was that 50% of their investment would be kept safely out of the market in a hedge fund. They stood to earn roughly 20% interest a month
Script “But it was Willie Breedt generosity that did it for Leon Schotlz.
Leon: I said to him I'm expecting money to become available at the end of October and I …...need for some extra monthly income. And he said that he can start up with hundred and fifty thousand for me as a start because I was unsure. And I thought This guy's ...putting his own money until my money becomes available on my name to start earning an income, that was giving me confidence
Script: Investors deposited bitcoin into Vaultage Solutions online wallets, which once converted into dollars. The bot would trade on various cryptocurrency exchanges. Investors got weekly emails confirming the 5% compound interest on their capital. Artist Anton Liebenberg left his investment to grow for nearly a year
Anton: I said to my wife this is just so easy. I mean we just invested in a 25 K. It has grown to about 90000. We just withdrew a lump sum of 45 why didn't we invest more
Link: Willie Breedt owns several companies including the Westrand News. His home in this upmarket estate, and his love of flash cars and Harley Davidsons inspired confidence in his business acumen.
Script: In 3 years over 2000 investors had put in about R224 million
Link: The other major player in this story is Anton Rogers, who until recently was a Liberty financial adviser, mandated to only to sell Liberty products. He recruited more than 750 people to invest in Vaultage Solutions, including his close family members.
Masa: Did Anton’s status as a Liberty Life Consultant give you confidence in his advice
Anton: Wholeheartedly, definitely. In the beginning he asked me what I must give my full year a pension fund to him.
Masa: He asked you to do that
Anton: I thank God I didn't
Script: Rogers in an email from his lawyer denies this and says it was solely the decision of Mr Liebenberg.
Script: Annette Veldsman has known Rogers for over 16 years
Annette: We did an annual review we looked at growth and we looked at the possibilities of good investments and he came up with a suggestion that he know someone very well which is now Mr. Willie Breet and basically told me of some magnificent growth thats sounded like a very good thing
Script: Annette chose for her weekly 5% interest to be deposited into a Luxpin card, the bitcoin is converted into cash and they can be used like global travel wallet. The cards can be swiped at stores and at an ATMs. The money babies were coming in and when it reached the 100 000 dollars Anton told her she had to open an offshore Isle of Man account, presumably to avoid tax

Annette: I had some money invested in portfolios at Liberty which he managed and I started withdrawing those investments the one it was eventually three hundred and fifty thousand rand …
Script: Rogers denies he encouraged Anette to close her Liberty policy.
Then in September 2019, the interest payments suddenly stopped. Initially blaming power outages, then system upgrades. But confidence was restored with a big year end party
Anton: I was actually surprised that a pay platform like this actually invite you for a year end function, you know these guys are legit.
Script: Liebenberg invested another R100 000- the marketing strategy clearly had paid off
Link: Willie and his family left Krugersdorp last year when things started to go wrong, and ever since then trying to get a straight answer about where their money is, has sent investors from pillar to post
Anette: Then we received emails that trading would stop..people are in a flat spin they don't know whether he's opted and packed the bags of money and left
Script: It turns out Willie had been holed at his mansion in this luxury estate in Jeffreys bay since January
Link: We came to his officers to try and find out more, but this is what we found, it's clearly been deserted
Script: And investors have been left hanging with endless promises.
Leon: Then I said to him Willie, in the name of Jesus Christ, are all our funds safe, and he said to me, in the name of Jesus Christ your funds are safe. That's the truth, the solid truth.
Script: Between Leon family and friends they have lost 4 million. He falsified proof of payments, Leon’s R654 000 turned out to be just R654
Horrified they learnt that Willie had done this before, he was the top recruiter for BTC Bitcoin global, a scam where 28000 investors lost over a billion rand
Annette “There were other people who knew about it but Willie sugarcoated his platform so immensely they thought well maybe he has made a turn in his life
Script:Investors hunted Willie down to his luxury hideaway in Jeffreys bay despite strict lockdown. This investor got him to hand over his luxury bikes and cars to settle his debt
Willie “When will you give over the vehicles for possession. If the payments don’t take place I will give it to him this afternoon”
Script: And recorded this explanation for other investors
Willie “In was just so sudden you know first the binance then the blockchain, couldn’t get any transactions through. I feel for every single member and that’s what people need to know and understand. Unfortunately things that were not in my control that happened”
Script: But Cryptocurrency expert Earle Loxton, says Willie’s explanations just doesn’t add up
Masa: What are you gathering what happened here
Earle: Let’s give Vaultage the benefit of the doubt. If in fact it was a trading algorithm bot it’s one of two things it's either a bot that was neglected or allowed to go haywire which basically means if it started losing money it wasn’t monitored .And the owner of the bot did not have his hand on it . The other possibility is obviously that these trades never existed the same funds of new investors being returned to the existing investors which is the definition of a posi
Masa: We talking 5 percent interest a week 20 percent a month, is this achievable anywhere in the world.
Earle: if you find it please tell me. You can understand it's something that's worth a lot of money. And the real programs are things that will cost you in the millions of dollars to develop. Many of the bots that you see out there look good on paper they trade well for a short time and then they go arye
Script: When pressed to prove if the money existed, Willie just forged the crypto statement
Anette “People were freaking out at this stage. You know especially that the ill people can't buy medication.. Pensioners buying food and then one day I just decided it has to stop somewhere. I arrogantly decided we need to take a legal route because everyone was threatening. Let's go to his house and break his legs. You know but you can't do that. I mean that's not the way to approach it
Script: Gordon Kayser has taken on the case and has found some of his clients weren’t even on the database
Gordon: most of my clients consist of pensioners that invested their money with Liberty and subsequently withdraw those investments on advice of Anton Rogers
Script: Gordon quickly found out that Willie had a fraud conviction with a 6 year sentence suspended for 5 , and had been in financial trouble since 2012. If 50% of the money was in a hedge fund he had to register it
Masa: Is it even registered with the financial information sector.

Gordon. He's not registered with the Financial Services Board giving people financial advice by investing their money. They have to be registered with the board not even to say that financial schemes act. You can get a fine of up to 10 million or 10 years imprisonment or both. I have done my research and voltage solutions is not registered with the fund.
Masa: In his explanation letter to his investors and he makes it explicitly clear that Voltage Solutions is not an investment company. Does this exonerate him?
Gordon: No not at all because he is still running the business of investing people's money
Script: We asked Liberty Life about their financial advisor Anton Rogers
Following a comprehensive investigation, Mr Rogers was found to have acted outside of his mandate with Liberty, and his contract was immediately terminated. Liberty further debarred Mr Rogers as a financial adviser and has been removed from the central register ….and cannot at this stage practice as a financial adviser in South Africa.
Script: Rogers denies this and says the matter is in arbitration for procedural unfairness. In general, he feels he has been harassed with defamatory statements
Script: Willie fled Jeffreys Bay alleging he had received death threats, and is now in deep hiding. In the interim, the court issued a preservation order against him.
Gordon: the preservation order basically means the bank accounts that we know of gets frozen and the assets are Mr. Breedt is being restricted of selling any assets including the assets in his family trust
Annette “I think 1st prise will be a conviction because someone like this can’t be just roaming the streets and just taking people money
Gordon Criminal proceedings have been instituted against Mr. Breedt and his accomplices. And the investigation is at the critical stage with the Hawks

Promo 11 sec “Investors are furious,the promise of 20% interest on their cryptocurrency investment went badly wrong. Over 2000 people are asking where their money has gone. Was this just another ponsi scheme
11 sec Over 2000 people were lured by a fantastic Bitcoin investment parting with their hard earned money. This collective online trading scheme made millions for some, until it went wrong.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Vaultage Solutions owned by Willie Breedt reputable businessman from Krugersdorp who also owned the local community newspaper Westrand News, a mansion in the upmarket estate of Featherbrooke Estate, and a drone business. Willie loves Harley Davidsons and smart cars and is a flash friendly guy. Since 2018 he’s convinced 2500 people to invest R227 Million in his Bitcoin Business. In December 2019 he threw a big end of year function to celebrate how well they were all doing, now he is holed up in Jeffreys bay and investors are no longer getting their weekly 5% interest pay-outs, never mind their original capital investments. Was this just another pyramid scheme gone belly up?
metadata.Summary: With the local economy looking more and more rocky it was a fail-safe investment because the trading was done by an ‘Automated Trading System’ programmed never to trade when the prices were down and half the money was in a hedge fund so nobody’s capital was at risk. Investors would earn 20% a month interest and they could withdraw 5% a week. Many people made good money over the last two years but then in September last year Willie started to pay people late and from January this year nobody is seeing any money just lots of empty promises. Initially investors thought he had left the country when he went to Mozambique in December and it was clear he had left Krugersdorp. Then he had a nervous breakdown and his wife asked investors just to be patient, holed up in Jeffreys Bay in another exclusive estate, a home which he bought for cash for R3.8 million but ensured he registered in a family trust is his bolt hole. Since April he has made a series of promises that he will pay out 70% of people capital investments, none of which have transpired. Fears that he may leave the country as soon as lockdown has eased has spurred 200 of the investors to hire an attorney who is bringing an urgent application this Wednesday 17th June.
metadata.Further information: The other major culprit in this scheme is Anton Rogers was a financial broker for Liberty Life has been advising his clients since September 2018 to move their Liberty investments into Vaultage Solutions. With several years’ experience and various financial degrees, you could trust his word. He convinced 774 of his clients including his mother, his cousins that Vaultage Solutions was a great way to increase your investments. He earned commission from Willie Breedt but when his clients confront him he says he is just another investor and also a victim. He was fired by Liberty Life in January 2020 and is now recruiting people to invest in the latest pyramid scheme Crowd 1. Anton lives in Pretoria. Willie Breedt has done this before, another financial investment scheme called MSM and Bitcoin Global which involved 23 billion rand went under and Willie was convicted of convicted on a criminal charge of fraud and was given a sentence of six years imprisonment, five of which are suspended . He is currently still on a suspended sentence which expires September 2020 and if found guilty again on another charge can go to prison for the full suspended term of 5 years. Vaultage solutions is not registered in terms of Section 5 of the Collective Schemes Control Act, 45 of 2002, with the Financial Sector and Vaultage Solution was only registerd as a company in April 2019 with Willie as the sole director. If you are convicted of fraud you cannot be the director of a company and seems like he only registered the company after trading for at least 6 months. In September when Willie started to pay out dividends later and later and it became apparent his data base was in complete disarray. By December he had left Krugersdorp for his house in Jeffreys bay. He has met several of his investors who drove to Jeffreys Bay to negotiate with him. We have a video of his negotiating with Dr Bertus Jansen van Vuuren that he will hand over his luxury cars if he can’t pay his debt.
